role: environmental prop — a hanging lantern, repeated across rooms to give the spaces depth and pooled light
note: Multi-image conditioning, NOT text. This request has no prompt field: the turnaround views carry the entire style. The views were generated from the pavilion's own exhibit art, which is what makes a generated prop congruent rather than merely plausible.

curation.purpose: First module of the pavilion kit. Proves the image-set pipeline end to end before it is spent on architecture.

reject: Not a single coherent lantern — merged blobs, doubled parts, or exploded geometry.
Contains lettering, numerals, or invented inscription.
Glass panes absent as distinct faces.
accept: One lantern with a readable hexagonal cage, tapered roof, and base finial.
Warm aged brass with visible patina.
Dim warm glass held as a distinct material from the metal.
Hangs plausibly from a ceiling and reads at room scale.
Sits in the measured palette without fighting the exhibit art.

passed: One coherent lantern — no merged blobs, doubled parts, or exploded geometry.
Readable hexagonal cage with six vertical corner posts.
Tapered hexagonal roof present, base finial present.
Warm aged brass with patina in the recesses; not chrome, not neon.
No text, lettering, numeral, or invented inscription.
failed: Glass panes read as OPEN AIR — no visible surface, thickness, or tint. Directly violates the accept tier requirement that glass be a distinct material from the metal. Retained geometry, lost material.
observations: PBR set confirmed produced: base_color, metallic, roughness, normal.
Fine ornament on the roof and upper band is smeared, consistent with reconstructing from two views.

Input views were only ~300-800 px before upscaling, which is the likely cause of the smearing. The sheet split a 1774 px width three ways; briefing TWO views instead gives each roughly half the width.
reviewLog.rootCause: Transparency is invisible in a still image, so translucent glazing arrives as nothing and reconstructs as nothing. The brief asked for translucent glass and therefore asked for this failure.
reviewLog.correctionApplied: Brief v2 demands OPAQUE FROSTED glass drawn as a solid matte surface, bolder simpler ornament, and two views instead of three for more pixels per view.

viewSelection: v2 sheet re-sliced after the generation process exited. First slice read the sheet at 09:13 while codex was still running (it exited at 911s and rewrote the file at 09:15), so the submitted views were stale and carried 22.3% magenta-family pixels - which baked into the material and returned a pink lantern. Re-sliced views measure 0.0% magenta. Slicer now refuses an input modified in the last 12 seconds.
